easy.def: A pretty stone that shows many colors.
examples: The opal is shiny.
She has an opal ring.
The opal shows many colors.

more.def: A smooth stone that shows flashes of many colors.
examples: The opal shimmered with green and blue.
Grandma wore an opal ring.
The opal looked different in the light.

easy.def: To move something so it is not shut.
examples: Open the door.
I opened the box.
She opens her eyes.

more.def: To move or take away something that is closed, so that things can go in or out.
examples: Please open the window to let in some fresh air.
He opened the gift and smiled.
The flowers open when the sun comes up.

easy.def: Not shut.
examples: The door is open.
An open box sat there.
The store is open.

more.def: Not closed, or ready for people to come in.
examples: The library is open every day except Sunday.
The open gate let the sheep wander out.
They slept with the window open on warm nights.

easy.def: A tool for opening cans or bottles.
examples: Use the can opener.
The opener is in the drawer.
I need a bottle opener.

more.def: A tool or device that is used to open a can, jar or other container.
examples: Dad used the can opener to open the soup.
The opener is in the kitchen drawer.
A jar opener helped Grandma twist off the tight lid.

easy.def: The first thing in a show or game.
examples: The first song was a great opener.
The opener was fun.
Our team won the opener.

more.def: The first act, game or event in a series.
examples: The first song was a great opener for the concert.
Our team won the season opener by three goals.
A joke is a good opener for a speech.

easy.def: A hole or gap.
examples: There is an opening in the fence.
The cave has an opening.
A small opening in the wall.

more.def: A hole or gap that something can go through.
examples: A narrow opening led into the cave.
The cave's opening was hidden by bushes.
The mouse slipped through a small opening.

easy.def: The start of something.
examples: The opening of the play.
The opening of the store.
Opening day is today.

more.def: The first part or time of something.
examples: The opening of the movie was exciting.
The new library had its opening on Saturday.
Opening day for the baseball team is in April.

easy.def: In a way that is honest and not hidden.
examples: She talked openly.
He openly said sorry.
They played openly.

more.def: In an honest way, without hiding anything.
examples: She spoke openly about how she felt.
He openly admitted that he had made a mistake.
They talked openly about their plans.

easy.def: A play where the actors sing the whole story.
examples: We saw an opera.
The opera was long.
She sings in an opera.

more.def: A play in which all the words are sung to music, usually with an orchestra.
examples: We went to the opera and listened to the singers.
The opera told a story through songs.
She dreamed of singing in an opera.

easy.def: To make a machine work.
examples: He operates the crane.
Can you operate the radio?
She operates the elevator.

more.def: To use or control a machine so that it works.
examples: He operates the crane at the dock.
Can you operate this camera?
A trained worker operates the crane.

easy.def: To cut into a body to fix it.
examples: The doctor will operate.
The surgeon operated on his knee.
They operate on animals.

more.def: To cut into a body in order to fix a problem.
examples: The surgeon will operate on his knee.
The vet operated on the injured dog.
Doctors operate to fix broken bones.

easy.def: Work done by doctors to fix a body.
examples: He had an operation on his knee.
Grandpa had an operation.
The doctor did an operation.

more.def: A medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body to fix a problem.
examples: My grandpa had an operation on his knee.
The doctor explained the operation to the family.
She stayed in the hospital after the operation.

easy.def: How a machine works.
examples: The operation of the machine is easy.
The robot is in operation.
The car's operation is simple.

more.def: The way in which something works or is run.
examples: The operation of the machine is simple.
The factory is in operation day and night.
She learned the operation of the new camera.

easy.def: A math step such as adding.
examples: Adding is an operation.
Subtraction is an operation.
Multiplication is an operation.

more.def: A math process, such as adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing.
examples: Addition is the first math operation we learn.
Division is the opposite operation of multiplication.
Each operation has its own symbol.

easy.def: Working and ready to use.
examples: The machine is operational.
The new bridge is operational.
The elevator is operational again.

more.def: Working properly and ready to be used.
examples: The machine is operational again after the repair.
The new bridge will be operational by spring.
The elevator is operational, so we do not have to take the stairs.

easy.def: Working or in use.
examples: The machine is now operative.
The rule is operative today.
The new bridge is operative.

more.def: Working, in effect or in use.
examples: The new rule becomes operative next Monday.
The old pump is no longer operative, so we use the new one.
The machine was operative again after the repair.

easy.def: A person who works a machine.
examples: The crane operator lifted the beam.
The phone operator answered.
A bus operator drove us.

more.def: A person who works a machine or a phone system.
examples: The crane operator lifted the steel beam.
A phone operator helped us find the number.
The train operator blew the whistle.

easy.def: What you think about something.
examples: In my opinion, pizza is best.
What is your opinion?
Her opinion is different.

more.def: What a person thinks or believes about something.
examples: In my opinion, dogs make the best pets.
What is your opinion of the book?
Everyone in the class gave an opinion.

easy.def: Always saying what you think.
examples: He is opinionated.
The opinionated boy talked.
An opinionated girl.

more.def: Having and sharing strong opinions, often without listening to others.
examples: The opinionated boy argued about every game.
She is so opinionated that she rarely listens.
An opinionated critic wrote the review.

easy.def: A person you play against.
examples: My opponent is tall.
The opponent won.
I shook my opponent's hand.

more.def: A person or team that you compete against in a game or contest.
examples: My opponent in chess was very good.
We shook hands with our opponents after the game.
The opponent scored a goal.

easy.def: A chance to do something good.
examples: This is a great opportunity.
I had an opportunity to swim.
Take the opportunity to rest.

more.def: A chance to do something that you want or need to do.
examples: I had an opportunity to meet the author.
The trip was a great opportunity to learn.
She took the opportunity to ask a question.

easy.def: To be against something.
examples: I oppose the plan.
She opposes the rule.
They opposed the change.

more.def: To be against something and try to stop it.
examples: I oppose the plan to cut recess.
The town opposed the new road.
She opposed the rule.

easy.def: On the other side.
examples: The opposing team won.
They sat on opposing sides.
The two opposing ideas.

more.def: On the other side in a game or an argument, or completely different from another idea.
examples: Our team shook hands with the opposing team after the game.
The two sisters had opposing ideas about where to go for dinner.
Two opposing groups sat on either side of the room.

easy.def: Something that is as different as it can be.
examples: Hot is the opposite of cold.
Up is the opposite of down.
Big is the opposite of small.

more.def: A person or thing that is completely different from another.
examples: The opposite of "ancient" is "modern."
He said he was tired, but he acted the opposite.
My sister is the opposite of me: she loves mornings.

easy.def: Hard to bear because it is so heavy or hot.
examples: The heat was oppressive.
An oppressive silence.
The air was oppressive.

more.def: Feeling very heavy or hard to bear, such as heat or rules.
examples: The oppressive heat made everyone tired.
An oppressive silence filled the room.
The humid air was oppressive.

easy.def: Having to do with the eye or seeing.
examples: The optic nerve is in the eye.
The camera has an optic lens.
The optic nerve helps you see.

more.def: Having to do with the eye or with sight.
examples: The optic nerve carries messages from your eye to your brain.
The optic lens in the camera is clear.
A doctor checked the optic nerve.

easy.def: Having to do with sight or light.
examples: We saw an optical trick.
The optical lens is glass.
An optical illusion fooled us.

more.def: Having to do with sight, light or lenses.
examples: The magician's trick was an optical illusion.
A camera has an optical lens that bends light.
The optical store sells glasses.

easy.def: Thinking that good things will happen.
examples: She had optimism.
He is full of optimism.
Optimism helps.

more.def: The habit of expecting good things to happen.
examples: She faced the test with optimism.
His optimism cheered up the whole team.
A little optimism helps on a gloomy day.

easy.def: A person who always expects good things.
examples: She is an optimist.
An optimist sees the good.
The optimist smiled.

more.def: A person who expects good things to happen and sees the bright side of things.
examples: She is an optimist and always thinks tomorrow will be a better day.
The optimist said, "It will stop raining soon."
An optimist sees a glass as half full.

easy.def: Thinking good things will happen.
examples: She is optimistic.
An optimistic girl.
He feels optimistic.

more.def: Expecting good things to happen.
examples: She felt optimistic about the test.
He is optimistic that it will be sunny.
The optimistic team believed they would win.

easy.def: A choice you can make.
examples: Pizza is one option for lunch.
You have two options.
Walking is an option.

more.def: One of the things you can choose from.
examples: The menu gives you three options for dessert.
Taking the bus is a good option when it rains.
We talked over every option before we chose a name for the club.

easy.def: Something you can choose to do or not.
examples: The extra reading is optional.
Wearing a hat is optional.
The trip is optional.

more.def: Not required, but left for you to choose.
examples: Wearing a costume to the party is optional.
The extra homework is optional.
Sprinkles on the ice cream are optional.
